title: Your Grandparents Wasted Almost Nothing
sendTrigger: Send this to whoever does the groceries.
editorialNotes: $2,913/yr is the EPA April 2025 household figure (sourced in gtm.json).

copy.headline: Your grandparents wasted almost no food. You waste $2,913 a year. What changed?
They were poorer than you.
items: They threw away less than you.

copy.headline: They shopped daily.
items: Bought what that day's meals needed.
Leftovers became tomorrow's lunch - not a virtue, a necessity.
copy.body: The fridge was small because it didn't need to be large.

copy.headline: Three things changed.
items: Fridges tripled in size (9 cu ft in the 1950s -> 22 today).
And food got cheap enough to feel disposable.
copy.citation: AHAM/DOE appliance data; USDA ERS Food Expenditure Series.

copy.headline: When food cost 30% of income, wasting it felt like burning money.
copy.body: At 10%, waste stops registering. A $4 bag of spinach doesn't feel like a loss. Multiply it by 52.

copy.headline: The irony: they were poorer and wasted less. You're richer and waste more.
copy.body: Abundance didn't solve the food problem. It made it invisible.

copy.headline: Your grandparents didn't have a system.
You don't need her budget. You need her visibility.
